Before we talk about software

You already have a system.
It's just not software.

A WhatsApp inbox, a diary, three Excel files and one person's memory. It works, right up until the day it doesn't. Does any of this sound like your week?

🔍

The enquiry you can't find

Serious budget, good conversation, back in March. You remember the chat. You don't remember the number.

The follow‑up nobody made

Not forgotten on purpose. Nothing reminded anyone. The file quietly closed itself, no decision ever made.

The quotation that ate the evening

Open last month's Excel, fix the totals, check the maths twice, export a PDF that still looks like Excel.

The business in one head

Off‑the‑shelf doesn't fit

Most CRMs are built for a forty‑person sales floor abroad, priced per head, forcing you to bend to fit.

None of this is a discipline problem. Everyone in this position is working hard. It's a tooling problem, and the tools built to fix it were never built for a business like yours.
Is this for you?

Built for one kind of business. Maybe yours.

It's for you if

  • You run a business of roughly 3 to 50 people
  • You sell through enquiries, quotations and follow‑ups, not a checkout page
  • Enquiries come in on WhatsApp, calls, walk‑ins, IndiaMART or referrals
  • You're a distributor, manufacturer, trader, dealer, interiors or furnishing firm, AV or industrial supplier

It's probably not for you if

  • You get fewer than 10 enquiries a month
  • Your team already uses a CRM properly, every day
  • You sell online at a fixed price, with no quotations

If that's you, I'll say so in our first chat and save us both the time.

Built by a business owner, for business owners

I run a business, like you. For years I was the one remembering everything: which enquiry came on WhatsApp, who was quoted what, who needed a call back on Thursday. When something slipped, I never even knew it had.

I tried the big CRMs. Good software, built for someone else's business. So I built one around how mine actually works, and my team has run on it every day since.

Now I set it up for a few other businesses, one at a time. I'd rather understand how yours works first than sell you anything.

Under the hood

Four things doing the work.

For those who like to know how. Each one exists because it cost my own business deals before it was built.

01

Quotations that win the room

Pick items from your catalogue and Kriya builds the whole proposal: cover, itemised products, specs and terms, on your own letterhead, in minutes. Whoever quotes first, and looks most serious, usually wins.

🎙 "Ramesh Iyer called today. Architect, referred by Mehta. Needs a quote for a new office this week."
✓ Contact created 🔥 Hot lead Referral tagged
📋 Paste a WhatsApp screenshot → a clear summary note on the customer's record
02

Say it or paste it. It's saved.

Speak for ten seconds and Kriya creates the contact, tags where they came from, and reads the urgency in your own words. Say it inside a customer's record and it becomes a note or a reminder there instead of a duplicate.

Paste a WhatsApp screenshot and the AI Engine turns the chat into a short, readable summary on that customer's record. No typing, no import wizard.

03

Follow‑ups that don't depend on memory

"Call him back Thursday" becomes a dated task for the right person, not a line in a diary. Every morning, your team sees who is due today, and you see which customers are about to go cold.

Due today
Mehta Traders: send revised quote · Priya
Nair Interiors: second follow‑up · Rahul
Going cold
3 quoted customers, no reply in 7 days
💬 Tap WhatsApp on a customer's record. Your own number opens with their chat, and the message is logged against them.
Your own number Saved templates API optional
04

WhatsApp, the way you already use it

Message a customer from their record on your own WhatsApp, with a saved template if you want one. Every conversation stays attached to the customer. If you later want automatic or bulk messages, the official API can be added. It's optional, not required.

More that's built in
  • Ask, don't filter. Type "Which quotations are still pending?" or "Dealers in Pune who haven't ordered in 60 days" and get the answer, including what's written inside notes.
  • A catalogue that gets smarter. Upload your price list and Kriya fills in images, descriptions and specs. Fix something inside a quotation and the fix flows back to the catalogue.
  • Your brand, not mine. Your logo, bank details, terms and team on every document. Nothing points back to Kriya.
  • Different pipelines for different customers. Regular leads, service requests and referral partners each move through their own stages.
  • Built around you. A custom field, a website form, something out of the box. If it helps your business run better, we'll build it.

Both are serious, capable products, built to suit every kind of business. Kriya is built for Indian businesses that sell through enquiries, quotations and follow‑ups, and it's set up around how yours already works: branded quotations built in, WhatsApp from your own number, and one flat fee instead of per‑user pricing.

Building a demo and running production software for a real business are different problems. The monthly fee isn't for the code, it's for someone who owns the hosting, fixes it when it breaks, keeps your customer data safe, and evolves the system as your business changes. That accountability doesn't disappear because building got faster.

Existing exports come in as part of setup, with contacts, notes and original dates preserved, not reset to today. If your records live only in WhatsApp or a diary, that's normal too; most clients start there and build up from day one.

Your data stays yours. It's accessed only to provide support you've asked for, never shared, and never used for any other client. Kriya runs on infrastructure built and managed for you, so problems get diagnosed and fixed directly, without ever asking for your password.

That's what the leak check and the free dashboard are for. You see your own business running on it before anything is agreed. If it's genuinely not a fit, that gets said plainly rather than taking your money and finding out together in month four.

Month‑to‑month from the end of the free trial, no long‑term lock‑in. Either side can end it with 30 days' written notice. If a payment is ever missed, you'll be contacted directly before any suspension of service.
